paraphrase: The naked ascetic Guṇa of the Kassapa clan teaches King Aṅgati: there is no fruit, good or bad, of living by dharma; there is no other world — who has come back from it?; there are no ancestors, no mother or father, no teacher to tame the untamed; beings are all equal, there is no honouring of elders; there is no strength or energy, still less effort; beings are fixed (niyatāni) like the stern-rope of a boat; a man gets what he is to get, so what fruit has giving? Giving was laid down by fools. Seven bodies are eternal and cannot be cut — fire, earth, water, air, pleasure, pain and soul — so the sword only passes between them; all are purified by wandering through 84 great aeons, and before that time even the restrained is not purified: 'we do not pass beyond destiny, as the ocean does not pass its shore'.
notes: Reported by an opponent: a Buddhist Jātaka (Ja 544 Fausbøll / SC ja545). SuttaCentral verse segments 34–45, checked locally.
